html:
Tiwanaku was a great city near the southern shore of Lake Titicaca, in today's Bolivia. At its height, from about 500 to 1000 CE, it ruled or influenced much of the southern Andes.

Its builders raised stone platforms and courtyards, with gateways such as the Gateway of the Sun, carved with a staff-holding god. Raised fields around the lake fed a large population, and llama caravans carried its goods as far as the Pacific coast and the eastern valleys. With the Wari state to the north, it was one of the first great states of the Andes.

A long drought around 1000 helped bring its fall. The Inca later treated the site as sacred. Today it is a symbol of the Aymara people, and Evo Morales took office there in a ceremony in 2006. The Tiwanaku state page tells more.
sum: Tiwanaku was a great city near the southern shore of Lake Titicaca, in today's Bolivia. At its height, from about 500 to 1000 CE, it ruled or influenced much of the southern Andes.
